searchText: I would also very much welcome a tool or documented approach which minimises errors for large number of validator deployments. I suspect that use case is too niche for there to be an officially supported method of doing so. **dankrad** I think those needing it should just fund one :) **dankrad** if you got millions of dollars to stake this should be worth it to you **svantemand** Sounds very reasonable. If you were the guy with the millions in Ether, how would you go about it? You could always spend your millions on a ultra-high-speed internet connection so you could download ethdo and ethereal _really_ fast. (You would still want to manually test the information generated, and if you used something else for your keys there may be additional hoops to jump through, but these tools do have the ability to do bulk deposits). If ethereal and ethdo do the job than this is fine then they should get more spotlight and testing. Sure it’s a niche requirement but these people will probably end up providing 80% of the stake. In my opinion we should cater a bit to early investors that still hold since genesis or maybe moved their Ether maybe once via the split contract after the DAO hack which could easily be millions today. They are the people who I trust will have no problem locking away their ETH for another 1-2 years as they are the most long term oriented. <@!291925846556540928> eth2 call tomorrow? oh yeah.. one minute! v comfy thank you! call tomorrow! https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/184
